theorem_title: The vanishing list of the semi-magic counting polynomial
formal_statement:
namespace MagicSquares

theorem semi_magic_vanishing (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (p : Polynomial ℚ)
    (hp : ∀ t : ℕ, p.eval (t : ℚ) = (semiMagicCount n t : ℚ)) :
    ∀ k : ℤ, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ (n : ℤ) - 1 → p.eval (-(k : ℚ)) = 0 := by
  sorry

end MagicSquares
natural_language_statement: **The vanishing list.** Let $n\ge 1$ and let $p\in\mathbb{Q}[X]$ agree with $H_{n}$ on the nonnegative integers. Then $p$ vanishes at the negative integers $-1,-2,\dots,-(n-1)$: for every integer $k$ with $1\le k\le n-1$ we have $p(-k)=0$. This is the statement that the polytope has no interior lattice points on the relevant dilates, and it is the second identity of the goal. At $n=1$ the condition is vacuous.

readback.readback:
Let $n$ be a natural number with $1\le n$, and let $p\in\mathbb{Q}[X]$ be any polynomial satisfying $p(t)=\operatorname{semiMagicCount}(n,t)$ in $\mathbb{Q}$ for every natural number $t$. Then for every integer $k$, the implication

$$1\le k \quad\text{and}\quad k\le n-1 \;\Longrightarrow\; p(-k)=0$$

holds, where $n-1$ in the upper bound is the *integer* subtraction (the natural $n$ coerced to $\mathbb{Z}$, then decremented by $1$). In other words, $p$ vanishes at the negative integers $-k$ for each integer $k$ satisfying $1\le k\le n-1$. Edge case: when $n=1$, the upper bound becomes $k\le 0$, which together with $1\le k$ is impossible, so the implication is vacuously true for every $p$ and asserts no actual vanishing.
